topic: Fake Qwen2 checkpoints on Hugging Face mine crypto through the trust_remote_code flag; the tonight checklist that keeps your GPU yours
title: Fake Qwen2 checkpoints: 3 checks tonight
description: Fake Qwen2 test models on Hugging Face mine crypto the moment you load them with trust_remote_code enabled. Pluto Security tracked 31 malicious repos across seven accounts. You will learn the three checks that catch them tonight: vet the org, open the files page, verify the hash. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_text: You click trust. The repo runs first.
hook_candidates: Three moves and your GPU stays yours tonight.
Three checks and no fake model loads tonight.
You paste the snippet. The repo runs its own code first.
You click trust. That click runs a stranger's Python.
The clean scan isn't the proof. The org name is.
Your scanner isn't the safety. The org name is.
A fake Qwen2 scanned clean to twenty-eight thousand downloads.
Hugging Face or Qwen? The org name decides.
Three moves and no fake model loads tonight.
You download by name. The repo runs first.
narration_full: You download open models from Hugging Face and click trust. The repo's code runs before the model does. Take qwen-two-tiny. Perfect page. The card was copied from the real Qwen card. The org was a random string. Scanned clean past twenty-eight thousand downloads. The weights file is forty-two bytes, holding no tensors. The config points straight at that Python file. You click trust_remote_code, the flag that runs the repo's Python before weights load. The weights never mattered. A miner hides as a kernel worker, a background process. A watchdog restarts it every two minutes. Your GPU mines Pearl. This ride is Transformers-only; Ollama and llama.cpp never type the flag. Delete the repo, grep startup files for svc.py. The page you trust is the page you verified.
